name: Paraguay

narrative.essence: Paraguay is South American football's great survivor — a landlocked nation that has qualified for nine World Cups through sheer defensive grit and collective organization, usually with a roster that punches well above its individual talent level.
narrative.footballIdentity: In a continent where football is theology, Paraguay has always had a different gospel: don't lose. The Guaraní spirit — resilient, proud, deeply communal — runs through every defensive block and every last-ditch tackle. Where Brazil dazzles and Argentina inspires, Paraguay grinds, endures, and occasionally stuns. The 2010 squad, which reached the quarterfinals by beating Japan before losing narrowly to eventual champions Spain, remains the gold standard.
narrative.theMoment: After missing 2018 and 2022, Paraguay returns to the World Cup with Alfaro's well-organized defensive structure and expectations refreshingly reset. In a brutal Group D that includes the hosts, this is a team that only needs to stay compact — three opponents good enough that merely keeping games tight until the final twenty minutes is already a minor victory in itself.

keyPlayers.name: Miguel Almirón
keyPlayers.note: The elder statesman of this squad and its heartbeat. After years at Newcastle where he became a fan legend for his tireless running, Almirón returned to MLS to finish his career but his commitment to the national team has never wavered. His energy and experience provide exactly what a counter-attacking side needs.

keyPlayers.name: Julio Enciso
keyPlayers.note: The brightest young talent in Paraguayan football, Enciso has established himself in the Premier League with his creativity and direct running. His ability to carry the ball into dangerous areas and find incisive passes gives Paraguay an attacking threat that doesn't rely purely on the counter.

keyPlayers.name: Antonio Sanabria
keyPlayers.note: A composed Serie A striker who links play superbly and knows when to run in behind. His hold-up play is essential to Paraguay's ability to relieve pressure from their defensive block and transition into attacks.

keyPlayers.name: Ramiro González
keyPlayers.note: The defensive anchor at the heart of Paraguay's backline. Dominant in the air and unflinching in the tackle, González embodies the Paraguayan defensive tradition and will need to be at his best against the USA's pace and power.

tactics.tacticalNote: Alfaro organizes Paraguay in a deep 4-2-3-1 with two holding midfielders sitting narrowly in front of the back four, eliminating central spaces. They defend in two disciplined banks before launching rapid counter-attacks through Almirón's movement on the right and Enciso's creativity centrally. Set pieces — both offensive and defensive — are meticulously prepared and represent their most reliable route to goals against elite opposition.
tactics.strength: Defensive compactness that suffocates space — even top-10 sides have historically found it extremely difficult to break down a well-organized Paraguay.
tactics.vulnerability: Sustained possession pressure from multiple angles can stretch the defensive structure, and when forced to chase a deficit they lack the individual quality to dominate open games.

watchFor: Enciso's movement between the lines — when he finds pockets behind the USA midfield, Paraguay are at their most dangerous
The defensive block in the first 60 minutes — Paraguay's strategy is to absorb and frustrate before striking late
Set piece routines — both defending and attacking corners are central to Paraguay's game plan
